newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan ends at new two-month high vs US dollar.
newsitem.headline: Yuan ends at new two-month high vs US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan ended at a two-month closing high of 8.2942 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai on Thursday for the second day in a row, up from Wednesday's 8.2945 due to speculative buying, traders said.
The close was the highest since February 21 when the yuan ended at 8.2940.
The weighted average price on Wednesday was 8.2946.

Dealers said speculative buying in the last 10 minutes of trading pushed the yuan to the high after it had moved in a narrow range just above the psychologically-important 8.2950 level for most of the session.
The yuan opened down at an intraday low of 8.2950 and stayed in the range 8.2945 to 8.2950 for most of the session before it rose slightly late in trading, hitting a high of 8.2940.
Trading was dull with most business done at about 8.2947, traders said.
One dealer said the speculative buying right before the close helped the yuan to hold above 8.2950.
"The yuan was under pressure to slide back below to the 8.2950 level, but the last-minute buying made it stand firmly above that psychologically-important level," he said.
Dealers said said they expected the yuan to move around the 8.2945 level on Friday.
The yuan on Thursday closed up slightly at 6.5615 from 6.5775 against 100 Japanese yen and little changed at 1.0710 from 1.0711 against the Hong Kong dollar.
